answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring stake-backed reputation that accrues slowly: a new identity, however light as a sparrow, starts with only a tiny trading limit and must complete verified, useful tasks to earn standing. Creating thousands of fake accounts gains nothing, because each must separately lock funds and build history, raising attacker cost linearly. A shared terrace of public attestations records performance, so Sybil clones cannot inherit trust, while misbehavior slashes stake and burns reputation like yarrow cut back before it spreads.
